main_text.p: bauimus[?]. Ego sum, inquit, apud prophetam faciens pacem & creans malum, malum sci licet pœnæ non culpæ. Totum enim hoc opus non causis secundis, non rebus naturalibus, non malitiæ hominum, sed Deo tribuendum est, qui his externis mediis efficaciter vti-tur, qui impios excitat, vt nos eorum manu castiget, (non enim malitiam illis inspirat, sed ea vtitur ad nos castigandos.) Dein secundo loco incommoda tantæ pœnæ enumerauimus, hoc est, quam dira ac horrenda sit demonstrauimus.

Sequitur vt tertio loco dicamus, quid nam Deum moueat, (qui clemens & miseri-cors est) vt tam horribili & dira pœna bonos æque ac malos, infantes perinde ac senes, vniuersas denique regiones ad-ficiat. Nec de his causis etiam sanum est mundi iuditium, sentiunt quidem omnes manum ferientis Dei, de pœna communis omnium querela est: At quia iuditio multi carent, & asinis stupidiores sunt, nec sentiunt nec intelligunt, quas ob causas id fiat, aut quomodo ex præsentibus his malis

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment "bauimus" (probably a verb ending such as peccauimus); the initial letter is uncertain. "vti-tur" and "miseri-cors" keep their printed line-end hyphens. The long s is transcribed as a plain s throughout (printed "fecundis", "fe-cundo", "sanum" read as secundis, secundo, sanum). Printed "medijs" is given as "mediis" and "iuditium/iuditio" is kept as printed. Printed "scilicet" is split across the line end ("sci / licet") and written whole.
